rounds.proof_sketch: total_elements = 16384 * 4096 = 67,108,864. block_size = 256. Original: (67,108,864 + 256 - 1) / 256 = 67,109,119 / 256 = 262,144 blocks. Mutant: (67,108,864 + 256 + 1) / 256 = 67,109,121 / 256 = 262,145 blocks. Since 67,108,864 = 262,144 * 256 exactly, original launches exactly the needed blocks. Mutant launches 1 extra block (256 threads). Extra threads have idx ∈ [67,108,864, 67,109,119], all failing the guard `if (idx < total_elements)`.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the grid size calculation from the standard ceiling division formula `(n + b - 1) / b` to `(n + b + 1) / b`. For the fixed input shape [16384, 4096], total_elements = 67,108,864 is exactly divisible by block_size = 256, yielding 262,144 blocks in the original and 262,145 in the mutant. The kernel has a bounds check `if (idx < total_elements)` that prevents out-of-bounds writes. All 256 threads in the extra block have indices >= 67,108,864 and are filtered out by this guard. Therefore, both versions produce bitwise-identical output for ANY input values. The equivalence is structural, not value-dependent.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects the number of launched thread blocks, adding one extra block whose threads are all filtered by the bounds check. No value-level input can distinguish the outputs because the computation for valid indices is identical in both versions.
rounds.recommendations: When testing mutations in grid/block size calculations, verify whether the bounds check inside the kernel creates semantic equivalence. For this specific fixed shape where total_elements is exactly divisible by block_size, any mutation that results in >= ceil(total_elements/block_size) blocks will be equivalent. To improve mutation testing coverage, consider testing with shapes where total_elements is NOT divisible by block_size, or mutations that could cause FEWER blocks than needed.
